:::{#exm-first-order-logic}
#### From "for all" to one element

Let $P(x)$ be a predicate about the elements of a set $S$,
and let $a \in S$.
The propositions $\forall x \in S, P(x)$ and $a \in S$
logically entail $P(a)$:
if $P(x)$ is true for every element $x$ of $S$,
then it is true for the element $a$.
For example,
$\forall x \in \mathbb{Z}, x^2 \ge 0$ entails $3^2 \ge 0$.
Propositional logic alone cannot express this entailment,
because it has no way to refer to the elements of $S$.

:::
